title: The Bremen Town Musicians
author: Brothers Grimm
source: Public domain. Retold from the Brothers Grimm.

characters.name: The Donkey
characters.voiceHint: a big, slow, friendly hee-haw voice

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, there was a donkey who had carried sacks to the mill for many long years. When he grew too old to work, he decided to run away to the town of Bremen.

segments.speaker: donkey
segments.text: "I shall become a musician!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he said, and off he trotted down the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Before long, he met an old hunting dog lying by the road, panting sadly.

segments.speaker: dog
segments.text: "I am too old to hunt, and no one wants me anymore."

segments.speaker: donkey
segments.text: "Come with me to Bremen! You can bang the drum, and I will play the lute."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The dog wagged his tail, and away they went together.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon they came upon a cat sitting in the road with a face as gloomy as three rainy days.

segments.speaker: cat
segments.text: "I am too old to catch mice, so no one will feed me."

segments.speaker: donkey
segments.text: "Come with us to Bremen! You know a fine tune or two. We shall all be musicians!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the cat joined them, and on they went.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At a farmyard gate they found a rooster crowing with all his might.

segments.speaker: rooster
segments.text: "Cock-a-doodle-doo! They mean to put me in the soup on Sunday!"

segments.speaker: donkey
segments.text: "Better to come with us to Bremen! You have a mighty voice — together we shall make music like no one has ever heard."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The rooster flapped up onto the donkey's back, and the four friends set off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Bremen was far away, and night fell while they were still deep in the forest. Then the rooster, from high in a tree, spotted a little light in the distance. The friends crept closer and found a cozy cottage — with a band of robbers inside, feasting at a table piled high with good things to eat!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The hungry animals put their heads together and made a plan. The donkey stood at the window, the dog climbed on his back, the cat climbed on the dog, and the rooster perched on top. Then, all at once, they made their music: the donkey brayed, the dog barked, the cat meowed, and the rooster crowed — and they crashed right through the window!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The robbers leapt up in terror.

segments.speaker: robber
segments.text: "A monster! A terrible monster is coming through the window!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they cried, and they ran out of the cottage and into the dark forest as fast as their legs could carry them. Then the four musicians sat down at the table and ate until their bellies were round and happy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Late that night, one robber crept back to take another look. But in the dark, the cat scratched him, the dog nipped his leg, the donkey gave him a mighty kick, and the rooster crowed from the rooftop. The robber flew back to his friends.

segments.speaker: robber
segments.text: "There is a witch in there who scratched me, a man with a knife, a giant with a club, and a judge on the roof shouting 'Bring the rascal here!' Never, ever go back!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the robbers never did. The four musicians liked the little cottage so much that they stayed there together — the donkey, the dog, the cat, and the rooster — making their happy music whenever they pleased. And as far as anyone knows, they are living there still.
